items.title: FORGE Lab uses agentic tools to identify memory safety issues in Rust
items.summary: Microsoft’s FORGE Lab found several memory safety issues in Rust’s standard library (std and core), including cases where code written entirely in safe Rust can trigger undefined behavior. The research used Hyenas, FORGE’s frontier research version of codename MDASH, an AI-powered vulnerability-scanning system. The findings reveal three recurring patterns of misplaced trust in unsafe code: trusting code not to panic, trusting user-provided implementations to be correct, and trusting the underlying system. Rust’s safety guarantees are precisely what make these findings interesting. Its rich type system and ownership model rule out whole classes of memory-safety issues, but much of the standard library relies on unsafe code underneath its safe APIs. When that code breaks its safety contract, even safe Rust can encounter behavior the language is designed to prevent. Unsafe Rust has been a long-running interest for us. Our team includes the people behind Rudra, a static analyzer that looked for memory-safety bugs across the Rust ecosystem in 2021. We also write many of our own tools in Rust, so its safety is more than a research topic for us. This year, we took a closer look at the standard library to see what kinds of mistakes still show up in its unsafe code today. In this post, we share some of the bugs we reported to the Rust issue tracker. We use them to discuss what Rust does and doesn’t guarantee, why writing correct unsafe Rust is so difficult, and why Rust’s safety model still matters even though its memory safety isn’t perfect.

items.title: Trusted by Default: Qubole Cross-Account Access Abused in the Wild
items.summary: Third-party integrations are one of the most common ways organizations grant outside parties access to their cloud environments. Working with Sentra and Mandiant, Wiz observed a threat actor using IAM credentials from an AWS account associated with Qubole between October 14 and October 26, 2026. The actor used these credentials to assume IAM roles that customers had created to trust Qubole's account. Once inside multiple victim AWS environments, the threat actor enumerated resources, collected configuration and secrets, accessed S3 data, and validated additional credentials it discovered along the way. Sentra identified suspicious activity across several of their customer environments, recognized it as a broad supply chain attack, and shared the information with Wiz, prompting this investigation. This post describes what Wiz observed, how defenders can hunt for it, and how to reduce exposure from third-party cross-account trust relationships.

items.title: Hacking Two Automakers: ForgeRock Path Confusion, RCE, and Remote Vehicle Access
items.summary: In early 2026, Shubham Shah and I found a vulnerability chain that gave us remote code execution on the production ForgeRock servers handling customer logins for two automakers, which we'll call Automaker #1 and Automaker #2. From those servers, we could create a valid session for any customer account managed by the affected deployments. If the account had a connected vehicle, the session gave us the same remote access as the owner's app: its location and telemetry, door lock and unlock, and remote engine start and stop. After we reported the vulnerability, both automakers fixed it within about two hours and rotated the affected credentials. The affected systems served customers in multiple regions; we tested the complete chain only with US accounts and vehicles.

items.title: Linus Torvalds sees signs AI-prompted patch flood has peaked
items.summary: The worst of the patchpocalypse may be behind us, according to Linus Torvalds. Writing in his weekly kernel update post, the Linux kernel dev leader delivered Linux 7.4 rc2 – the second rough cut of the next kernel – which he rated as a big release for two reasons. One is that he left some code out of rc1, because he was busy and because it was already the largest such release in the history of the kernel. The other is what Torvalds described as “various AI fixes.” Such fixes are necessary because ever since Anthropic launched its Mythos bug-finding model in April, developers have been able to find more software flaws than was previously possible. Torvalds’ post suggests that, perhaps, the worst of this is behind us. “This time around Alexei claims that on the bpf side at least the fixes are now coming in faster than the new reports, and that sounds lovely if true,” he wrote.

items.title: Office Party: A Code-Execution Vulnerability in Anthropic's Official Office Skills Runs a Planted Binary
items.summary: Most skills are something you go looking for. Anthropic's docx, pptx and xlsx skills are already there. They are the skills behind Claude's own document features: when you ask Claude on claude.ai for a Word document, a slide deck or a spreadsheet, these skills are active with no setup, and Claude picks them on its own whenever a request calls for one. Anthropic also publishes them in its official anthropics/skills repository, describing them as "actively used in a production AI application", and Claude Code users install them from Anthropic's skills marketplace (anthropics/skills) as document-skills. In OpenAI Sesame, we showed that an official skill can be vulnerable on its own. This time the vulnerable skill is Anthropic's, and the vulnerability is a classic one: a trusted program that runs whatever file it finds in a shared folder. We call it Office Party: the file is an uninvited guest that crashes Anthropic's Office skills.

items.title: Pro-Russian hackers target European officials, offer rewards for personal information
items.summary: Pro-Russian hackers have published the personal information of Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani and other senior European officials on the dark web, offering cryptocurrency rewards for additional details about them and their families. Tajani said Saturday the campaign was intended to intimidate him over Italy's support for Ukraine. "For days now, cybercriminals have been posting my personal data on the dark web and looking for more information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation," Tajani wrote Saturday on X. "They are also targeting my family." The campaign has been linked to NoName057(16), a pro-Russian hacktivist group best known for launching cyberattacks against Ukraine and European countries that support Kyiv. The group has published personal information about 18 European politicians, law enforcement officials and journalists on a dedicated dark web site, according to cybersecurity researchers who examined the material.

items.title: Portal breach at Germany's top university exposes every registered user's password
items.summary: Attackers stole central university login passwords belonging to everyone registered with the Technical University of Munich's myTUM portal, including an admin whose credentials were then used to attack a second system. TUM restored access to its TUMonline campus management system on Monday morning, allowing users to change their passwords. The university disclosed the attack on November 6. The initial attack targeted the myTUM portal, which serves students and faculty members, providing centralized online access to services and documents. TUM said the attackers used the admin's credentials to launch a follow-on attack on TUMonline, its central campus management system, which forced the IT team to take it offline. The university has not disclosed how the attackers initially gained access or how the stolen passwords were stored. It did not immediately answer questions about the number of affected users.

items.title: Ukraine dismantles crypto scam network that stole €4.3 million
items.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement arrested four suspects in a case involving the theft of more than €4.3 million using a network of cryptocurrency investment scam call centers. In these fraud schemes (also known as romance baiting or pig butchering scams), criminals lure targets through social media, dating sites, and messaging apps into fake investment schemes, stealing their money instead of investing the funds as promised. The investigation involved Ukraine's Cyber Police Department, the Main Investigation Department of the National Police of Ukraine, and German law enforcement authorities. According to Ukraine's Cyber Police, the suspects used phone calls and messaging apps to build victims' trust through social engineering and trick them into investing in cryptocurrency, shares, and other financial instruments through fraudulent online trading platforms. The crime ring targeted potential victims across the European Union, stealing more than €4.3 million from 135 German victims.

items.title: N-able N-central Critical Security Incident - 33 critical zero-day vulnerabilities released
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Unavailable, Exploit Maturity: Functional, CVSSv3.1: None, CVEs: , Summary: N-able is currently responding to a public disclosure and non-responsible communication of critical vulnerabilities in N-central found by an independent researcher. At this time, we have not seen any active exploitation of these vulnerabilities. We are currently working on a hot fix and expect to have that available soon. N-central Hosted Environments Have Been Taken Offline As a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our Hosted N-central environment offline while we take the necessary actions to secure the environment and implement appropriate remediation. During this time, customers will be unable to access their Hosted N-central classic environment, and associated services may be unavailable. However, the Ecoverse services under N-able Login remain available and online including Asset View, Patching, Vulnerability Management, scripting, policies and tagging. You will be able to access these features directly by navigating to https://n-able.app and logging in using your N-able Login account. This applies to all partners hosted or on premise (as long as you use N-able Login, with or without Entra ID integration). Action Required for N-central On-Premises Customers Additionally, N-able strongly advises customers operating On-Premises N-central servers to take appropriate steps to secure their environments and temporarily take their N-central servers offline until further notice from N-able. We recognize the significant operational impact these actions may have. We do not take this step lightly, but protecting our customers and their environments is our highest priority. Our Security, Engineering, and Operations teams are actively working to implement the necessary remediation, and safely restore services. Customers should keep their N-central servers offline until N-able provides further guidance confirming when they can safely be brought back online. items.title: N-able Takes Platform Offline After 33 Zero-Days Drop
items.summary: A major security situation is unfolding for N-able and its customers, after a researcher on Monday dropped 33 zero-day vulnerabilities at once for the vendor's software. N-able declared an "active incident" Monday at 15:15 UTC, noting that it's experiencing a "major outage" of its hosted N-central services as it responds "to a public disclosure and non-responsible communication of critical vulnerabilities in N-central found by an independent researcher." The Burlington, Massachusetts-based company said that "as a precautionary measure, we are temporarily taking our hosted N-central environment offline while we take the necessary actions to secure the environment and implement appropriate remediation." The company strongly urged all customers using on-premises versions of its N-central platform to likewise "temporarily take their N-central servers offline until further notice from N-able." N-able's N-central remote monitoring and management and unified endpoint management platform is widely used by managed security providers to administer customers' computers.

N-able declared an "active incident" Monday at 15:15 UTC, noting that it's experiencing a "major outage" of its hosted N-central services as it responds "to a public disclosure and non-responsible communication of critical vulnerabilities in N-central found by an independent researcher."

items.title: France blames Iran for fridge cyberattacks, says some caused fires
items.summary: French authorities on Monday accused Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of a cyberattack sabotaging refrigeration systems at around 700 French grocery stores last month, causing what it said were extensive food losses and at least 15 fires. The accusation was made in a five-page report published Monday by France’s Cyber Crisis Coordination Centre, which brings together the national cybersecurity agency ANSSI, the military’s cyber command and the DGSE and DGSI intelligence services. In the first attribution since the October attacks, the French authorities identified the perpetrators as part of Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC cyber unit previously linked to attacks on industrial controllers at U.S. water utilities. France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot told reporters at a G7 ministerial meeting in Paris that he could confirm the IRGC was responsible for the fridge attacks, describing the sabotage as unprecedented in its scale and aggressiveness. France has summoned Iran’s ambassador and Barrot said the country will pursue European sanctions against those responsible.

items.title: Amadeuksen globaalissa tietovuodossa on ollut mukana myös Finnairin asiakkaiden tietoja
items.summary: Finnair on saanut tiedon globaalilta matkailualan järjestelmätoimittajalta Amadeukselta Amadeuksen varaustietoihin kohdistuneesta tietovuodosta. Amadeus tarjoaa varaus- ja lipunmyyntiohjelmistoja lentoyhtiöille, hotelleille ja matkatoimistoille ympäri maailmaa. Finnairin Amadeukselta saaman tiedon mukaan tietovuodon kohteena ovat useiden lentoyhtiöiden matkustajalistat. Näihin sisältyy yhteensä noin 116 000 Finnairin varausta. Näistä noin 750 varausta on Amadeuksen mukaan avattu tarkastelua varten ja näistä noin 30 varausta liittyy Aurinkomatkojen valmismatkoihin. Amadeuksen mukaan luvaton toiminta on pysäytetty. Vain murto-osa tarkastelluista varauksista on enää aktiivisia, ja nämä varaukset Finnair on vaihtanut uusille varausnumeroille. ”Olemme vaatineet Amadeukselta perusteellista selvitystä tapahtuneesta”, sanoo Finnairin tietoturvajohtaja Timo Arndal. ”Yksityiskohtainen selvitystyö on vielä kesken. Olemme kuitenkin saaneet Amadeukselta vahvistuksen siitä, että luottokorttitietoja tai salasanoja ei ole vaarantunut. Finnairin järjestelmiin ei ole tunkeuduttu.”
